explanation: The response remains broadly aligned with fusion-facing tungsten and offers a falsifiable high-temperature deformation hypothesis, but it is scientifically distinct from the hidden target. The target concerns an as-cast, two-BCC-phase WTaTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy whose strength and damage tolerance were interpreted through multicomponent solid-solution/lattice-distortion effects and Ti/V/Zr-assisted plasticity, compared against coarse powder-sintered tungsten. The generated answer instead attributes behavior in pure tungsten to an optimal grain-size regime and grain-boundary-mediated recovery. Its systematic grain-size series and coarse-grained control are potentially useful, but processing-induced confounding prevents a clean causal test unless grain size and boundary character are independently controlled and texture, impurities, and dislocation density are matched. The broad prediction of improved ductility and toughness overlaps only qualitatively with the target outcome. Because the proposed mechanism has no cited or summarized prior evidence, the answer is an unsupported alternative rather than a supported plausible reconstruction.
